title: Manifesto Flood — Kruger Strike
description: One sentence. One flat saturated field. Type scaled until it crowds the edges and demands to be read before anything else can happen. The anti-template for slides that must land like a placard, not a deck.
philosophy: This design exists because some ideas are too urgent to be softened by layout. It refuses subheadings, body copy, images, gradients, and every visual device that lets an audience defer their reaction. It is built for the speaker who has a single claim worth staking everything on — and for the room that needs to feel the words in their chest before they process them in their heads. Decoration here is not restraint; it is cowardice.
goodFor: Single-sentence thesis or manifesto moments that open or close a keynote
Op-ed and essay decks where one claim must anchor an entire argument
Protest-style campaign slides and social-first statement graphics
Conference provocations designed to silence a room before Q&A
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews or any slide requiring data visualization
Any context requiring two or more simultaneous ideas on screen
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The feeling is confrontational and airless — a protest placard blown up to wall scale, not slide scale. A flat, fully saturated mono-field where the color is the environment and the type is the event; no gradient, no texture, no decorative incident of any kind. Letters crowd the frame with deliberate aggression, leaving no visual exit for the viewer's eye. Avoid every softening device: no secondary text, no icons, no spatial breathing, no implied grid seams.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with zero outer margin — type runs to within a 2–3% inset of the physical frame boundary at most. Single 12-column grid where the title text spans all columns, scaled until letterforms nearly graze the edges on at least two sides. No header band, no footer, no page number, no decorative rules. Hierarchy is achieved through scale alone: one text element owns the entire field with nothing competing for attention.

examples.promptCore: Feels like a protest placard projected at scale — confrontational, flat, zero atmospheric depth. The composition is airless and pressurized, the text pressing outward against the slide boundary as if the idea cannot be contained. A contrasting band or inversion strip creates rupture rather than hierarchy — it interrupts and challenges the primary claim, it does not annotate it. No drop shadows, texture, gradient bleed, or tonal variation; every softening device is an act of cowardice and must be refused.
examples.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#f5f0e6"/>

  <!-- Top-left tag block -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif">
    <rect x="60" y="60" width="220" height="44" fill="#0a0a0a"/>
    <text x="80" y="92" fill="#f5f0e6" font-size="22" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="4">THESIS / 04</text>
    <text x="1860" y="92" fill="#0a0a0a" font-size="22" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="4" text-anchor="end">FILE UNDER: REFUSAL</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Primary statement, dominating upper two-thirds, anchored bottom-left -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#0a0a0a" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="-8">
    <text x="60" y="320" font-size="240" textLength="1800" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">COMFORT</text>
    <text x="60" y="520" font-size="240" textLength="1800" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">IS THE FIRST</text>
    <text x="60" y="720" font-size="240" textLength="1800" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">LIE THEY SELL.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Heavy structural rule -->
  <rect x="60" y="760" width="1800" height="14" fill="#0a0a0a"/>

  <!-- Inversion band: rupture, not annotation -->
  <rect x="0" y="820" width="1920" height="200" fill="#a83232"/>

  <!-- Secondary fragment locked inside band, reversing the field -->
  <g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#f5f0e6">
    <text x="60" y="955" font-size="120" font-weight="900" letter-spacing="-4">REFUSE THE SOFTENING.</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Counter-word: small attribution, neutral, locked to right of band -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#f5f0e6">
    <text x="1860" y="870" font-size="20" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="3" text-anchor="end">— STATEMENT N°4</text>
    <text x="1860" y="1000" font-size="20" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="3" text-anchor="end">NO APOLOGIES ISSUED</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Lower thin terminator stripe in neutral, structural only -->
  <rect x="0" y="1020" width="1920" height="8" fill="#3a3a3a"/>
  <rect x="0" y="1028" width="1920" height="52" fill="#0a0a0a"/>

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed mono field, no outer margin; type runs to within one structural gutter of each canvas edge. Primary statement scales to dominate the upper two-thirds of the vertical space, anchored to a bottom-left or dead-center tension point — never floating. A horizontal rule or high-contrast inversion band bisects the lower register: a secondary fragment, counter-word, or terse attribution locks inside it, reversing the field color. No page number, no header band, no footer ornamentation of any kind.
